Theory
Three ingredients:

SMART MASK

Due to the outbreak of COVID-19, a face mask has help us to reduce the spread of the COVID-19 viruses. The use of the mask has been substantially increased. For further enhancing the functionality of the mask, it is desirable for developing a smart product with an integration of digital technologies, including IoT, AI, mobile devices, and cloud computing. The smart product has the following features to minimize the spread of the COVID-19:
· Monitor and record the air quality of the surrounding;
· Notify users if the surrounding air quality is not acceptable;
· Keep track of the user's geolocations for facilitating a easy identification of suspected users;
· Publish the potentially hazardous areas to the users after analytics of collected data;
· Can be used for many times with an appropriate replaceable filter; and
· Reduce environmental pollution.
As a result, the proposed smart mask would help building a safe and green community.

SMART DESIGN

The smart mask is washable and reusable for multiple times. Only the replacement of the air filters is required to maintain the best functionality of the air purification. A sensor for measuring the air quality is equipped in the smart mask. Therefore, the user can be notified whenever the quality of air falls below the standard by using a cloud-based platform and a mobile app and thus avoid staying in an environment with stale air. Moreover, the smart mask can be used as a normal mask by removing the sensor part.

WHY IS IT BETTER THAN A REGULAR MASK?

In the past few months, mask waste has been increased, which has resulted in the increase of plastic pollution. However, one of the characteristics of the smart mask is that it can be reused multiple times. They can be washed by water and used for several months. After a few times of use, only the air filters need to be replaced for consistent clean air; but it still contributes tremendously to the environment.

SCAN THE QR CODE TO FIND OUT MORE

DETACHABLE COVER
Used to hold the air filters.

SENSOR HOLDER
This allows the sensor to be in place and to not fall off when the mask is being used.

FACE COVER
Used to place the sensor and has holes to allow air to pass through for a person's breathing.

AIR FILTER
The air will go through the air filters for purification. This reduces the risk of getting infected and helps the user to be cautious of the environment they are in.

SENSOR
2 air quality sensors to measure
• ambient air quality
• filtered air quality
A uVC LED to sterilize the inside of a mask after filtration. Once the filtered air quality becomes lower than the standard, LED will light up to inform the user. Additionally, there is a Pulse Oximeter board which monitors the user's oxygen-saturation and heart-rate.

SMART MASK

Due to the outbreak of COVID-19, a face mask has help us to reduce the spread of the COVID-19 viruses. The use of the mask has been substantially increased. For further enhancing the functionality of the mask, it is desirable for developing a smart product with an integration of digital technologies, including IoT, AI, mobile devices, and cloud computing. The smart product has the following features to minimize the spread of the COVID-19:
· Monitor and record the air quality of the surrounding;
· Notify users if the surrounding air quality is not acceptable;
· Keep track of the user's geolocations for facilitating an easy identification of suspected users;
· Publish the potentially hazardous areas to the users after analytics of collected data;
· Can be used for many times with an appropriate replaceable filter; and
· Reduce environmental pollution.
As a result, the proposed smart mask would help building a safe and green community.

SMART DESIGN

The smart mask is washable and reusable for multiple times. Only the replacement of the air filters is required to maintain the best functionality of the air purification. A sensor for measuring the air quality is equipped in the smart mask. Therefore, the user can be notified whenever the quality of air falls below the standard by using a cloud-based platform and a mobile app and thus avoid staying in an environment with stale air. Moreover, the smart mask can be used as a normal mask by removing the sensor part.

WHY IS IT BETTER THAN A REGULAR MASK?

In the past few months, mask waste has been increased, which has resulted in the increase of plastic pollution. However, one of the characteristics of the smart mask is that it can be reused multiple times. They can be washed by water and used for several months. After a few times of use, only the air filters need to be replaced for consistent clean air; but it still contributes tremendously to the environment.

SCAN THE QR CODE TO FIND OUT MORE

DETACHABLE COVER
Used to hold the air filters.

SENSOR HOLDER
This allows the sensor to be in place and to not fall off when the mask is being used.

FACE COVER
Used to place the sensor and has holes to allow air to pass through for a person's breathing.

AIR FILTER
The air will go through the air filters for purification. This reduces the risk of getting infected and helps the user to be cautious of the environment they are in.

SENSOR
2 air quality sensors to measure
• ambient air quality
• filtered air quality
A UVC LED to sterilize the inside of a mask after filtration. Once the filtered air quality becomes lower than the standard, LED will light up to inform the user. Additionally, there is a Pulse Oximeter board which monitors the user's oxygen-saturation and heart-rate.

FUTURE DEVELOPMENT

The data from the smart mask can be sent to the user's mobile phone so that they can keep track of their surroundings.

GUINNESS
WORLD RECORDS

How did we mimic the fish tail?
The scotch yoke mechanism is used to mimic the tail movement of the fish. Initially the motor used to get stuck when it reached the 0 and the 180 degree position, since there would be no horizontal force component to move the mechanism.
This problem was solved by adding a bearing on the mechanism for the smaller fish and changing the geometry of the mechanism in the bigger fish.
The bearing will allow the mechanism to change the angle due to it's ability to roll. The mechanism needs to just need to get out of the 0 and 180 degree positions to move.

How does the fish turn?
The fish is turned left or right by controlling the tail movement through precise encoder readings. The absolute encoder has 1024 steps to give very high accuracy. To turn, the speed of the tail is adjusted in between a full cycle - tail going from one extreme to the other. When the fish receives instruction from the controller to turn it moves relatively faster from one extreme end (point A) to the other (point B). The arduino continuously updates the encoder value at fixed intervals and when the encoder returns a value which signifies point B the power is made lower depending on a value known as the turning differential. This turning differential can be controlled by commands through the controller and determines the sharpness of the turn.

Design is the most important thing?
To achieve the best performance, various types of tails were designed and tested. The details are shown to the left. To balance the buoyancy and improve the stability of the fish, the top and bottom fins were designed to be hollow inside. Therefore, it can be tested by adding and reducing the weights in it for the desired buoyancy.

What problems did we have?
The rotary motion of the motor is converted to a linear motion allowing the fish to move left and right. Being underwater, the force needed to propel the fish forward is large. The power provided from the Arduino microcontroller to the motor will not be sufficient. Hence, we have used motor drivers to allow for higher powered motors. The microcontroller will send PWM signals to the motor driver. A battery will be connected to the motor driver and it will be the source of power for the motor. The driver will compare the signals from the microcontroller such as off and on, and then regulate the power from the battery to the motor accordingly. The current fish uses a motor driver that we have built from scratch. However, we intend to upgrade the driver to allow for higher powered motors and for a more reliable system. We have tried using professional servo drivers such as the ESCON 70/10, but it is too large to fit into the body of our fish. The electronics team is currently working on a more compact motor driver.

Applications
- Search and Rescue
- Marine Exploration
- Hazardous and Plastic scrap detection

1
Introduction

Triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) is a new promising energy harvesting
technology that can produce electrical energy. A TENG makes use of the
coupling effect of triboelectrification to convert mechanical energy into
electrical energy. This project aims to design and fabricate a wearable
TENG that can be mounted on the human body as the electrical power
source of electronics. With the aid of energy harvesting technology, a
self-powered load-suspended backpack is developed and it can detect
shoulder misalignment. Meanwhile, the load suspended system allows the
reduction of vertical oscillation during the walking motion.

Functional block diagram

The load suspension system consisted of the elastic material, the load, and
the frame. The load is suspended while the frame is not. During walking,
the center of mass of the body goes up and down such that upward and
downward forces are exerted on the backpack accordingly. Meanwhile,
the elastic bands decouple the synchronous motion of the backpack such
that load tends to remain in a stationary position. The system can reduce
the 30.33% of vertical oscillation. Meanwhile, relative sliding motion is
achieved between the plate and the frame. The generated mechanical
energy allows the TENG to generate electrical energy.

4
Triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG)

Basic TENG configuration

Small deformation
Large deformation

deformation of brush

A TENG consists of two dielectric materials and they are connected to a
circuit. When two bodies are brought into contact, triboelectric charges are
induced on the surfaces. After separating the two materials, a potential
difference is induced between the two electrodes. To maintain electrostatic
equilibrium, the electron tends to flow to the other side through the external
circuit and current is induced. In our design, Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)
and nylon brush are adopted. Compared with the traditional design, the
brush-type structure allows deformation such that the surface contact area
increases and facilitates the power generation of TENG. A multi-layered
pattern is also adopted in the design to improve performance. The TENG
can generate 1.912 W in 20 minutes.

Shoulder misalignment detection design

Working principle of the detection system

Unlike the convention detection systems, the design involved no microprocessor
and sensors. A white Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) pipe is bent into 10-degree form to
a V-shaped structure. Clamped. Both interiors of the caps and the pipe are pat-
tached with copper tape for electrical conduction. A steel ball is also placed
inside. When the user exhibits shoulder misalignment, the backpack is tilted such
that the steel ball is rolled to the side due to gravity. The steel ball acts as a switch
and completed the circuit of the system by touching the cap and pipe at the same
time. As a result, the electrical energy generated by the TENG is discharged and
actuates the LED to warn the user. With such a design, the system only consumes
0.32 W and it fulfills the power supply of TENG.

HKU Robomaster
A competition-based platform for innovative young engineers

Competition & Goals

Robomaster is a national robotics competition for university students, hosted by DJI during the summer vacation on a yearly basis. It combines technology and e-gaming competition style, thus being exciting and unconventional.

The path to victory consists of the following steps:
• Form a development team by recruiting technical and managerial members
• Develop a team of auto or semi-auto robots, each with their own functions and restrictions
• Engage in showdowns with other teams of robots. On the battlefield, complete tasks to gain advantage; fire projectiles to lower the HP of enemy robots. A 0HP enemy base is a victory for your team.

HKU Robomaster Team has been recruiting enthusiastic engineering students since 2017. We aim to cultivate the quality of members that will benefit their career with the practical experience gained during the preparation and participation process. Our work is divided into technical management, mechanical & hardware management, and software & algorithm development.

Figure 1. The map of Robomaster battlefield

Mechanical & Hardware designs

The mechanical and hardware design of each robot is based on detailed planning. For each of the robot, we prepared the following technical files before turning concepts into reality:
• Requirement list
• Mechanical layout & actuation plan
• Hardware schematic

The following are the examples of our design. They are:
• Standard (top left): an agile robot on the ground that delivers moderate firepower and smart detection features
• Sentry (top right): a fully auto robot running on a rail near the base. Its firepower is for defense
• Hero (bottom left): A heavy robot dealing the most damage with special projectiles
• Engineer (bottom right): A utility robot that fires, rescues slain robots and delivers special projectiles to the Hero robot

Figure 2. The designs of robots

Technical Management

Technical management is meant to maximize the efficiency of development. It should also regulate the development so that it proceeds in a more orderly way.

The efforts we made this season include:
• Training courses, which offers a set of necessary technical and methodology knowledge.
• Archive system, which governs the naming and organization of development files.
• Documentation system, which specifies the technical details that can be referred to during development to minimize confusion.
• Team building activities, like team T-shirt and logo design. These help build the atmosphere in the team and enhance solidarity.

Algorithm development

To ensure victory, it is expected that the robot can be controlled accurately. Smart features like detection and prediction with computer vision are also favorable.

For software and algorithm design, we also come up with detailed plans before development. The plan is known as software structure, which specifies the overall logic and key technical aspects within each step and node. Testing is carrier out for fine-tuning.

RoboFish

Presented by BREED HKU – bio-inspired robotics organization at the University of Hong Kong

Aim

This project aims to provide an opportunity to explore the field of biomechanics and biomimicry.

Our current objective through this endeavor is to learn about the biomechanics of fish and other underwater organisms. The purpose is to understand how the movements are affected by different variables: speed, turbulence, drag, buoyancy. The model can be applied in surveillance systems and the study of marine biology.

Figure 1. Initial Design.

Hardware

RoboFish is controlled by a raspberry pi and powered by a battery.

The raspberry pi sends signals to the DC motor that moves the tail horizontally. However, since the motion of the DC motor is rotational, a mechanism was designed by the mechanical team to translate the rotational motion of the motor to a horizontal motion. In the future, more features such as remote controlling and surveillance systems aim to be added.

Software

Programming language used: C#. Coding in Unity.

Current stage:
Skeleton code for the fish working.
Skeleton code for the controller.
Background research on simulators.

Next stage:
Incorporating a simulator to simulate the environment of the swimming pool (the trial test environment for the model).
Through simulation, variation of different parameters of the fish to analyze which conditions provide best speed and energy efficiency.

Design

The goal is an ideal fish model mechanically designed to possess the following characteristics:
Streamlined body.
Minimum drag, especially at the edges and in the gaps between separate components.
Low weight.
Floating stability and buoyancy.

Figure 2. Basic Circuit Components.

Conclusion and Applications

We believe that there are several applications of our project for research in the academic world. Our model can be used to analyze marine biology through exploration of the sea. A significant possibility is thus the application of surveillance systems, not just in ecosystems research, but also in the navy.

BUDDY

DOODLE

Doodle relieves psychological distress by expressing emotions. It can also help in memory retention, which can be useful during reflection.

FYP19013: Early Diagnosis of Scoliosis in Children from RGB-D Images Using Deep Learning

Supervisor: Dr. Kenneth K.Y. Wong      Second Examiner: Dr. Loretta Y.K. Choi

Team Members: Li Gengyu (3035331886), Huang Siyi (3035335349)

ABSTRACT

Scoliosis is a medical condition where a person’s spine has a sideways curve. It usually occurs before puberty and prevents the lungs from functioning properly in severe cases. Scoliosis is typically diagnosed from X-ray images, but diagnostic X-rays increase the risk of developmental problems and cancer in those exposed. This project aims to obviate children’s X-ray exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis by generating X-ray images of children’s backs from the corresponding harmless RGB-D images rather than capturing the X-ray images directly from the children. An RGB-D image of a back combines a standard RGB image with its depth image, and the depth image consists of the distance between each point on the back and the camera to track the spine. In this project, a deep learning model based on HRNet was built and trained to detect landmark locations of the backs on the RGB-D images first. With the detected landmarks, the X-ray images of the children’s backs were eventually synthesised from the corresponding RGB-D images by another deep learning model that was built and trained based on the pix2pix model.

METHODS AND MATERIALS

Data Collection: captured RGB-D images and anatomical landmarks with Microsoft Azure Kinect DK from Duchess of Kent Children’s Hospital and performed data preprocessing.

The Mechanism of the HRNet.

HRNet: a state-of-the-art deep learning model for landmark detection tasks.

X-ray Synthesis: built and trained a deep learning model based on the pix2pix model to synthesize X-ray images from the RGB-D images and detected landmarks.

The Mechanism of the pix2pix Model.

The pix2pix model: a generative model based on conditional Generative Adversarial Network for image-to-image translation tasks.

INTRODUCTION

This is a deep learning project that aims to synthesize X-ray images of children’s backs from the corresponding RGB-D images to eliminate children’s radiation exposure in the early diagnosis of scoliosis. This project includes three main phases, data collection, landmark detection, and X-ray synthesis. The main deliverables are two deep learning models based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis, respectively.

Implementation Details

Landmark Detection:
Input: 4-channel RGB-D images.

X-ray Synthesis:

Ground Truth & Output: X-ray images.

Results and Analysis

Detected Landmarks:

Synthetic X-ray Images:

Sample Pairs of Ground Truth (left) and Synthetic (right) X-ray Images.

CONCLUSION

With the two deep learning models for landmark detection and X-ray synthesis based on the HRNet and the pix2pix model, this project achieved its goal of generating X-ray images of children’s backs from their corresponding RGB-D images with satisfactory results.

The BMFA Payload Challenge
The British Model Flying Association (BMFA) is the United Kingdom's National Governing Body for the sport of model aircraft flying and one of its key aims is to increase interest in aviation and engineering through education.

Canard Airplanes
Unlike conventional aircrafts with a tail, canard airplanes benefit from weight reduction due to reduction in overall length of the airplane and reduction in Lift force required. Design, Build and Fly

Summary
With the ever-growing demand for air cargo capacity comes the pursuit for cargo aircraft that combine a large payload with optimum efficiency. The Design, Build and Fly (DBF) team set out to meet this challenge by creating a radio-controlled model airplane, to compete in the Payload Challenge organized by the British Model Flying Association (BMFA). The process involved careful research into aeronautical engineering theories and creative solutions. The effectiveness of the design was proved in test flights by two fully functional prototypes. Various issues were identified during the trials, carefully examined, and subsequently addressed in an iterative manner. The team has continuously implemented modifications to the design, in an effort to produce the model plane that would carry the target payload with the highest efficiency attainable, and the results will hopefully provide useful insights for future model builders and aircraft engineers alike.

Competition Rules
The competition, "Challenge 4 – Quantity" of the BMFA Payload Challenge, requires all participating teams to design, construct, and fly an "electric powered, radio controlled aircraft", to "transport the greatest number of 150 ±1 10mm diameter polystyrene spheres of mass 35± /- 5g (see Figure 1) around a predetermined course (Figure 2) in the three 6-minute time slots utilising a standardised propulsion unit [1].

To verify the design concept, the first prototype was designed on a 1:2 scale.
Feedback collected from the first flight test contributed to the modification of the design, leading to a full-scale second prototype fully compliant with the competition requirements.

Two flight tests were carried out on 19 Feb 2020 (1st prototype) and 23 March (2nd prototype) at Hong Kong Model Engineering Club's (HKMEC) model plane airport in Yuen Long, Hong Kong.
The first prototype crashed immediately after take-off during the first trial. After improvisatory modifications were made on site, the test was able to continue.
The first prototype completed two successful flight cycles, justifying the feasibility of the design.
Issues identified were fed into the design of the second prototype. Major improvements included a more streamlined fuselage, larger wings, strengthened landing gear, adjusted motor placement and improved tail shape.
While some issues persisted and new problems were identified, the second prototype was overall a success and ready to be used in the competition.

Background

Usually, if we would like to measure something at home,
there can be some very large professional device, or we
can use some small liquid level meter (also known as
gradieter). However, such kind of level meter is not ideal -
the precision can be low as you are reading where the
bubble is.

Other approaches, like a digital level meter, which can
display exact values of the gradient degrees, is not
desirable enough due to its high price and difficult
operations. So for this project, I am thinking if we can make
a digital level meter and something more inside SenseHat
to use it, make it intuitive and particularly when we DIY
something at home.

SenseHat is a fascinating piece of hardware. It has all kinds
of sensors, and an IMU included. Through reading IMU and
other sensors' readings, we can show intuitively on the the
screen of SenseHat the result we are measuring.

Low precision

[image of low precision device with red circle]

More on IMU

IMU, abbreviation for Inertial Measurement Unit, measures
and reports a body's specific force, angular rate, and
sometimes the orientation of the body. IMUs are typically
used to maneuver aircraft (an attitude and heading
reference system), including unmanned aerial vehicles
(UAVs), among many others, and spacecraft, including
satellites and landers.

An inertial measurement unit works by detecting linear
acceleration using one or more accelerometers and
rotational rate using one or more gyroscopes. Some also
include a magnetometer which is commonly used as a
heading reference. Typical configurations contain one
accelerometer, gyro, and magnetometer per axis for each
of the three vehicle axes; pitch, roll and yaw. SenseHat
uses a library called RTIMULib to implement the interface
for reading from its IMU.

[small circular image]

Function Implementations

Func 1: Digital Level Meter

This function is similar to that offered in iOS's measure app. As
there is a tiny gyroscope inside SenseHat, we can read pitch
and roll values from the board. When the program detects that
roll is bigger than 45 or smaller than -45 degrees, the program
will switch to pitch measure mode. In this mode, a line will be
displayed and will turn green if SenseHat is placed horizontally.
When roll is between -45 and 45°, the program will switch to
pitch and roll measure mode. There will be two circles
displayed on SenseHat, and they will become closer if pitch
and roll approach zero. When zero is reached, the two circles
will collapse into one and the display will turn green, meaning
that SenseHat lies flat on a surface.

To draw lines programmatically on SenseHat, I have also
written a library called sensehat_graphic. The implementation

SenseHat comes with a compass, so we can know which direction
is North or South by setting two small dots on the border of the
screen. We can also know how many degrees we have turned. By
reading the change of yaw value, we can visualise it on the display.
This is also similar to the feature in compass app in iOS. Pressing
joystick once, it will set a base yaw value, and then it shows the
degrees increased/decreased. Press the joystick again to reset.

OUR PROJECT AIM

This project aims to design and build a fabric roll edge extractor
to replace the practice of labor operation in this procedure. The
fabric roll edge extractor will extract an adhesive tape from a roll
of fabric within 1 minute in an all-dry process. Full automation
processes can be replaced with the actual model in the current
human production line thus reducing operation cost and
human errors with higher efficiency.

OUR PROJECT SOLUTION

The device was divided into four mechanical processes
including tape locating, loosening, removing, and disposal,
respectively. After an array of research and analysis, we decided
to use a diffuse sensor for tape sensing, heat guns for tape
loosening, hook for tape removing, and pressurized air gun for
disposal.

FUTURE IMPROVEMENT AND DEVELOPMENT

1. Vertical axis actuation of the extractor
2. Replacement of the sensor
3. Integrate the location of fabric edge with NFC module
4. Tape disposal with pressurized air nozzle
5. Setup a database for different fabric materials

Build a new email client.

Limitation and Future Work

3. System overview
Capture chessboard image -> Remove background -> Find lines and intersection points -> Analyze canny edge and intensities of square -> Obtain piece color and location (PCL) -> Feed chess engine
[Below this flow are five small images of board states corresponding to each step; captions below each image are the same short phrases as in the flow: "Capture chessboard image", "Remove background", "Find lines and intersection points", "Analyze canny edge and intensities of square", "Obtain piece color and location (PCL)"]

4. Visual Recognition
Board Lines and Corners
- Using line algorithm
- Applying KMeans cluster to split lines into a horizontal group and a vertical group
- Calculating intersection points formed by each pair of points from these two groups.

Piece Location and Color
- Occupancy of squares is determined by counting the number of canny edges on the square.
- Analyzing the intensity histogram of occupied squares
- Determining piece colors according to the peaks of the intensity histogram.

Move
- Constructing a chessboard matrix (PCL) which records the board occupancy and the color of pieces.
- Obtaining piece moves by finding changes from the last PCL to the current PCL

5. Hardware
- Arduino Mega 2560 together with a RAMPS 1.4 Board and A4988 motor Drivers installed on it
- 3 stepper motors controlling robotic arm and pointer in x, y and z axes.

Player are in a role of villain, and they are required to control the spider-like robot (Hexapod) to explore the virtual fort augmented by AR in order to capture the princess.

Map Generation by Plane Detection

Plane detection in ARCore is enabled to look for clusters of feature points for environmental understanding, so that the game can create an anchor point on the detected horizontal flat surface when the players click on the screen. ARCore tracks the position of the anchor over time, the map will seems to be fixed on the floor as a result.

Robot Recognition by Image Tracking

Image recognition is enabled to track the referenced images pre-built in the database, so that the game can recognize the image stuck on the body of hexapod. The 3D eyes model of the hexapod will be augmented onto the robot for interacting with the virtual augmented terrain.

Hexapod Connection and Control

Classic Bluetooth with SPP is used to establish the connection between the mobile phone and the Arduino-based hexapod. Formatted Bluetooth commands are sent out for movement control at a regular time interval of 0.2 seconds to balance the time given to hexapod for response and the number of commands missed.

Movements like walking, picking up items, actions for celebration and different kinds of fighting actions are used in the game.

Gameplay

Players are required to explore the map by controlling the hexapod. Items collections are needed for solving the puzzle gameplay and increasing character's ability to combat with the enemies. OTE is added for the fighting system and 3D effects are augmented to the hexapod.

Players may receive the assistance from the spy in form of shop system in the mid-way of capturing the princess.

Competition & Goals

Robomaster is a national robotics competition for university students, hosted by DJI during the summer vacation on a yearly basis. It combines technology and e-gaming competition style, thus being exciting and unconventional.

The path to victory consists of the following steps:
• Form a development team by recruiting technical and managerial members
• Develop a team of auto or semi-auto robots, each with their own functions and restrictions
• Engage in showdowns with other teams of robots. On the battlefield, complete tasks to gain advantage; fire projectiles to lower the HP of enemy robots. A OHP enemy base is a victory for your team.

HKU Robomaster Team has been recruiting enthusiastic engineering students since 2017. We aim to cultivate the quality of members that will benefit their career with the practical experience gained during the preparation and participation process. Our work is divided into technical management, mechanical & hardware management, and software & algorithm development.

Figure 1. The map of Robomaster battlefield

Technical Management

Technical management is meant to maximize the efficiency of development. It should also regulate the development so that it proceeds in a more orderly way.

The efforts we made this season include:
• Training courses, which offers a set of necessary technical and methodology knowledge.
• Archive system, which governs the naming and organization of development files
• Documentation system, which specifies the technical details that can be referred to during development to minimize confusion.
• Team building activities, like team T-shirt and logo design. These help build the atmosphere in the team and enhance solidarity.

Algorithm development

To ensure victory, it is expected that the robot can be controlled accurately. Smart features like detection and prediction with computer vision are also favorable.

For software and algorithm design, we also come up with detailed plans before development. The plan is known as software structure, which specifies the overall logic and key technical aspects within each step and node. Testing is carrier out for fine-tuning.

beneficial to our society. For instance, its biomimetic nature doesn't interfere
with marine life like other underwater vehicles with turbines.
Not only is the new model much more energy efficient, less polluting, but it is
also environmentally friendly as it is constructed with less material.

Limitless Underwater Motion Control
• The robot consists of 3 main control protocols: the Roll, Pitch and Yaw.

Feedback system and PID control of the high-torque servo motor. A DIY
controller with simply input from joysticks and a potentiometer is developed to
provide accurate and quick control of the robot. With the aid of a suitable
configuration for our RC set-up, we have achieve a range of 10m for
communication.

Professional in manufacturing and waterproofing
• Mimicking a fish-like streamlined shape, the drag from the surrounding water
current is reduced.
• With a new, specialized design, we are able to achieve 100% waterproofing with
3D printing only.
• The reinforcement with stainless steel rods has given us sufficient rigidity to
overcome the oscillation produced by high-speed travelling.
• The complex bearing system at the tail section has ensured a smooth motion
with a very low energy loss.

for at least 24 hours, while also being able to support the fish for a service time
of at least 2 months.
